c: Bronze production began in the Middle Mumun and became increasingly important in ceremonial and political society after 700 BC.

c: The Bronze Age in Korea is often held to have begun around 900–800 BC, though the transition to the Bronze Age may have begun as far back as 2300 BC.

c: In 194 BC, the King of Gojoseon was overthrown by Wi Man (also known as Wei Man), a Korean-Chinese refugee from the Han vassal state of Yan.

c: Jolbon Buyeo was the predecessor to Goguryeo, and in 538, Baekje renamed itself Nambuyeo (Southern Buyeo).

c: Goguryeo was the first Korean kingdom to adopt Buddhism as the state religion in 372, in King Sosurim's reign.

c: Goguryeo initiated the Goguryeo–Wei War by attacking a Chinese fortress in 242 in an attempt to cut off Chinese access to its territories in Korea.

t: Baekje founded by Onjo
c: Baekje was founded by Onjo, a Goguryeo prince and the third son of Jumong, the founder of Goguryeo, in 18 BC.

t: Silla attacks Tang forces in Korean peninsula
c: Silla attacked Tang forces in Baekje and northern Korea in 671.

t: Silla defeats Tang invasion forces
c: Tang then invaded Silla in 674 but Silla drove the Tang forces out of the peninsula by 676 to achieve unification of most of the Korean peninsula.

t: Yi Seung-hyu includes Balhae in Korean history

t: Later Baekje founded in Wansanju
c: Later Baekje was founded by the general Kyŏn Hwŏn in 892, and its capital was established in Wansanju (modern Jeonju).

t: Later Baekje attacks Gyeongju
c: In 927, Later Baekje attacked Gyeongju, the capital of Unified Silla, and placed a puppet on the throne.

t: Kung Ye founds Later Goguryeo
c: Later Goguryeo was founded by the Buddhist monk Kung Ye in 901, and its original capital was established in Songak (modern Kaesong).

t: Later Goguryeo renamed Majin
c: Later Goguryeo's name was changed to Majin in 904, and Taebong in 911.

t: Yuan Shikai becomes resident in Korea

t: British Royal Navy occupies Geomun Island
